capabilities: parse natural-language date expressions typed after a trigger and replace them with the date
insert dates in built-in or user-defined format presets
turn a text selection into an aliased daily note wikilink
pick a date in a calendar picker and insert it as text, a link, or by opening the daily note
parse date expressions in six languages including relative phrases and times
disambiguation: Not a calendar or journaling plugin; it only inserts dates and daily note links at the cursor.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later. States no network connections or telemetry; parsing and formatting run locally via chrono-node and Luxon. Four settings require a plugin reload to take effect. BRAT and manual installation, the full user guide, and troubleshooting are documented outside the README. Some languages have known parsing gaps (Portuguese, Japanese, Dutch).
problem: Writing a date mid-sentence means counting on your fingers, consulting a calendar, or hand-typing wikilink syntax with the pipe and alias.

relations.evidence: Prior art — what the @ trigger owes to Natural Language Dates by Argenos
the core Daily Notes plugin, which Date Helpers relies on for the path and format of every daily note link

summary: Keyboard-first date insertion plugin that parses natural-language expressions like @next monday inline and inserts them as text or daily note links.
